body:
I would keep this PR limited to just the compat mechanism, and maybe 1 uncontroversial change to demonstrate it in practice. I'm not sure if `log` is actually uncontroversial, see my other comment.

Either way, I would not add several such changes _in the same PR_ -- it dilutes the discussion about the compat mechanism with arguments for/against concrete APIs being extended. A separate PR on the other hand can be reviewed independently.

This change is also mentioned neither in the PR title nor its description.

Did you measure the performance of this, when invoked with the default argument?

There's a very good chance that `std::log(e)` is not optimized away -- especially since the number literal isn't specified precisely enough -- which would mean that _every_ `log(x)` call now incurs an additional logarithm + float division operation. This would make GDScript `log` slower across the board, even for functions that don't use `base` (i.e. all usages up to now).
Could you add some comments what the individual parts here are doing?

Furthermore, there's also the risk of introducing numerical imprecision -- previous results of `log(x)` may no longer be the same after this change, especially if `log(e)` turns out not to be exactly 1.

Given how centrally `log` may be depended upon, I feel like this is a case where a separate function with a `base` parameter would be the better option. (Unless there's a way in GDScript to dispatch depending on presence of the argument).

Thanks for the review!

Since the log change is controversial I'd be more than happy to make a new PR without that.

I was originally working on this for is_zero_approx, see this issue/PR:
github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4425
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104408
However, I didn't use this one in the first place because this is only for the is_zero_approx part of that proposal.

So
Option 1: new PR with is_zero_approx as a proof of concept, leaving is_equal_approx as TBD
Option 2: new PR with only implementation and no POC
Option 3: figure out what to do with is_equal_approx and roll this into a fix for that entire issue... IMO that one really needs function overloading for a good fix though (like log lol)

and see my other comment RE scripting support.

the randfn change comes from this PR allowing for default arguments: (which I did mention in the description but maybe could have called out better)
PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/95017

that PR is required for script compatibility, but it isn't necessary for just gdextension compatibility, I could make a new PR without it but any proof of concept will be necessarily limited to only gdextension and not scripts.

see my other comment for further....

I don't want to get bogged down with log, I agree that it probably wasn't the best choice, but to answer your questions,
I did verify that log(e) returns exactly 1 (0x3FF0000000000000)
I didn't measure performance at all, I agree it is very doubtful anything is optimized there.

RE register_utility_function_compat
this is all a copy/paste from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112290
When you register the compatibility function, it's the same as the regular register_utility_function, but instead of adding the function to the utility_function_table, it adds it to a separate list of compatibility functions with the same name.
When the function is looked up for binding (variant_utility.cpp:2008), it first grabs the function from the original utility_function_table, then checks the function signature hash to see if the function signature is a match. If it's not a match, it looks through the registered compatibility functions and finds one that has the right function signature, and returns that one instead.
